motion.capture_method: Real local run of the installed product on this workstation: `singularity` resolved to /Library/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/3.12/bin/singularity and driven through a real pseudo-terminal (PTY) on macOS 26.4.1 (25E253) arm64, recorded as an asciinema v2 terminal cast with the timings of the run. The session issued only read-only commands — version form, top-level help, one subcommand help surface, one deliberately invalid flag, Ctrl-C on an unsubmitted line, the recovering help, and the same help with NO_COLOR=1 — from an empty scratch working directory. No host was contacted, no credential minted, no vault written, no job submitted and no service restarted.

interactions.name: command entry
interactions.trigger: Type `singularity --version` at the `wisent-ref$` prompt and press Enter.
interactions.response: Singularity starts from /Library/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/3.12/bin/singularity and writes to the pseudo-terminal.
interactions.cancellation: Ctrl-C on the unsubmitted `singularity --wisent-reference-probe` line discarded it and restored the prompt; nothing was submitted.
interactions.failure: `singularity --wisent-reference-probe` reaches the same parser and is refused with status 1.
interactions.evidence: media/session.cast at 0.000387–14.2265 s; observed exit 1; media/01-version-identity.png

interactions.name: version identity
interactions.trigger: Ask the installed binary what it is with `singularity --version`.
interactions.response: Singularity has no version flag: it refuses the option with status 1 and answers with its usage surface instead.
interactions.cancellation: The version form returns on its own; Ctrl-C is available at the prompt.
interactions.failure: The version request itself is the failure: exit 1.
interactions.recovery: Read the identity out of `singularity --help` instead.
interactions.evidence: media/session.cast at 0.000387–14.2265 s; observed exit 1; media/01-version-identity.png

interactions.name: help discovery
interactions.response: Singularity prints 3 lines of its own top-level help, widest line 73 characters.
interactions.cancellation: The stream is short enough to complete; the prompt stays interruptible.
interactions.failure: A misspelled flag on the same surface is refused with status 1.
interactions.evidence: media/session.cast at 14.4367–34.2084 s; observed exit 1; media/02-help-surface.png

interactions.name: subcommand surface
interactions.response: argparse gives every subcommand its own help; `onboarding` is the only one.
interactions.cancellation: Ctrl-C at the prompt abandons the request before submission.
interactions.recovery: Return to `singularity --help` for the documented grammar.
interactions.evidence: media/session.cast at 34.4141–55.2593 s; observed exit 1; media/03-subcommand-help.png

interactions.name: invalid flag refusal
interactions.response: Singularity refuses the unknown option and returns status 1.
interactions.cancellation: The refusal returns immediately; no cancellation was required.
interactions.recovery: The refusal names no next action; `singularity --help` recovers anyway.
interactions.evidence: media/session.cast at 55.4673–77.9833 s; observed exit 1; media/04-refusal.png

interactions.name: exit status reporting
interactions.trigger: After each command the recorded shell prints `printf "exit-status=%s\n" "$?"`.
interactions.response: The real status of the preceding product invocation appears in the cast as text.
interactions.feedback: exit-status=1 after the version form, exit-status=1 after the invalid flag.
interactions.cancellation: The status line is a shell builtin write; there is nothing to cancel.
interactions.failure: A missing status line would mean the prompt never returned; every step reported one.
interactions.recovery: Not applicable: the status is evidence, not an action.
interactions.evidence: media/session.cast at 14.2265–14.2265 s and after every other command

interactions.name: cancellation
interactions.trigger: Type `singularity --wisent-reference-probe` and press Ctrl-C instead of Enter.
interactions.response: The pending line is discarded and the prompt returns; the product never ran.
interactions.feedback: A fresh prompt follows the interrupt in the cast.
interactions.cancellation: Ctrl-C is the observed cancellation mechanism for unsubmitted input.
interactions.failure: The typed command is abandoned on purpose rather than executed.

interactions.name: recovery
interactions.trigger: After the refusal and the cancellation, run `singularity --help` again.
interactions.response: The same installed binary prints valid help and returns status 1.
interactions.cancellation: The recovery can itself be interrupted with Ctrl-C at the prompt.
interactions.recovery: The valid help form completes the first-success journey.
interactions.evidence: media/session.cast at 79.0159–98.4093 s; observed exit 1; media/05-recovery.png

interactions.name: color-free equivalence
interactions.response: The help text differs from the colored run once color is removed (3 lines).
interactions.feedback: 0 ANSI colour sequences in the default run, 0 with NO_COLOR=1.
interactions.cancellation: Ctrl-C at the prompt applies here as to any other command.
interactions.failure: No failure on this path; it is a measurement of the same success route.

motion_analysis.trigger: Enter pressed on each typed command in the recorded pseudo-terminal session; the seventh keystroke sequence is Ctrl-C instead of Enter.
motion_analysis.start_state: An empty `wisent-ref$` prompt in /Users/lukaszbartoszcze/.stado/work/wisent-capture/run/singularity with no product state, no credential and no target selected.
motion_analysis.end_state: The prompt restored after `NO_COLOR=1 singularity --help`, with the shell's own `exit-status=` line as the last product-related output.
motion_analysis.continuity: One append-only text stream: no screen clear and no cursor addressing appear anywhere in the cast, so every state reached stays visible above the next one and the whole journey can be read as one scroll.

accessibility.measurement_method: Measured from this run: SGR sequences counted in the raw PTY bytes, the same help command run again with NO_COLOR=1 and the two ANSI-stripped texts compared, the refusal text searched for a named next action, and the widest help line counted against 80 columns.
observations: Colour: with TERM=xterm-256color on a real pseudo-terminal and NO_COLOR unset, `singularity --help` emitted 0 ANSI SGR sequences, so this product does not colour its help output.

NO_COLOR: `NO_COLOR=1 singularity --help` printed 3 lines with 0 SGR sequences; the ANSI-stripped text of the two runs is not identical, so the two runs are recorded as different rather than equivalent.
Refusal wording: the refusal for `singularity --wisent-reference-probe` does not name a next action anywhere in its output.
Terminal width: the widest line of `singularity --help` is 73 characters, so the help fits an 80-column terminal without wrapping.
Input: the whole recorded journey is keyboard-only — typed commands, Enter and one Ctrl-C — and every state is emitted as selectable terminal text, not as a drawn widget.
State without colour: success and refusal differ by exit status in the cast (1 against 1), which the shell prints as text.
unknowns: Screen-reader behaviour was not observed: no screen reader was attached to this PTY.
Colour contrast of any emitted colours was not measured, and no WCAG or terminal-accessibility audit was performed.
Behaviour in a terminal narrower than 80 columns was not observed; only the emitted line widths were measured.
High-contrast themes, non-UTF-8 locales and alternative fonts were not exercised.
Authenticated and target-selected paths were deliberately not run, so nothing here describes the product's accessibility once a host, vault, queue or credential is involved.
